html:
An Iranian religious leader, born Husayn Ali Nuri to a noble family in Tehran, who founded the Baháʼí Faith.

He became a follower of the Báb, a young merchant who in 1844 announced a new revelation and was executed in 1850. After a failed attempt by some Bábís on the life of the shah in 1852, Baháʼu'lláh was thrown into a dark underground prison in Tehran and then exiled from Qajar Iran to Baghdad, then part of the Ottoman Empire.

In Baghdad in 1863 he declared that he was the messenger the Báb had foretold. The Ottomans moved him on to Istanbul, Edirne and finally the prison city of Acre in Palestine in 1868. He spent the rest of his life there and nearby, writing books and letters, among them the Kitáb-i-Aqdas, his book of laws, and letters to rulers of the day.

His teaching held that God is one and that the great religions come from the same source. He called for the unity of humankind, world peace, and later Baháʼís stressed the equality of women and men. His shrine near Acre is the holiest Baháʼí site. Baháʼís in Iran have suffered persecution from his day to ours.
sum: An Iranian religious leader, born Husayn Ali Nuri to a noble family in Tehran, who founded the Baháʼí Faith.
